text: Gold fell about 1.1% to near $3,905 overnight, giving back much of Monday's rebound as higher oil revived inflation worries and traders put a December Fed hike at about 75%.
Silver dropped about 3.4% to $48.93, back below $50, and the gold/silver ratio widened to about 79.8 from 78.
Brent rose about 1% to near $105.87 after a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, with Iran saying a deal is far off, partly reversing Monday's 7.6% drop.
Stock futures were mixed: Nasdaq 100 futures up about 0.3% and S&P 500 futures down about 0.1% at 8:29 AM ET, as Apple fell premarket on a weaker holiday-quarter margin outlook.
The 10-year Treasury yield edged up about 2 bp to 4.91% and the 2-year about 1 bp to 4.59% as voters went to the polls.
The dollar rose to about 158.2 yen, close to the 158–158.5 zone where traders watch for Japanese intervention.
NRGU closed Monday down 14.4% at $63.61 as oil plunged on hopes for US–Iran talks.
